scenes.title: RIGHT JOIN
scenes.narration: A RIGHT JOIN keeps every row from the right table and fills the left-side columns with NULL when no match is found.

scenes.title: What RIGHT JOIN guarantees
bullets: Every row from the right table is kept.
Left columns are filled in when a match exists.
Left columns become NULL when there is no match.
scenes.narration: Every row from the right table is preserved no matter what. When a matching left row exists, its columns are filled in. When no match exists, the left-side columns are set to NULL instead.

scenes.title: RIGHT JOIN is a mirror of LEFT JOIN

left.title: LEFT JOIN
points: NULLs appear on the right side.

right.title: RIGHT JOIN
points: NULLs appear on the left side.

scenes.narration: A right join is simply a left join reflected across the ON clause. Where a left join anchors on the left table and pads the right with NULLs, a right join anchors on the right and pads the left. The two are structurally identical apart from which table is guaranteed.

scenes.title: All departments, even empty ones
scenes.code:
SELECT e.name, d.dept_name
FROM employees AS e
RIGHT JOIN departments AS d
  ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id;
scenes.narration: Here departments is on the right, so every department is returned even if it currently has no employees. Departments that do have employees produce one row per employee with the name filled in. A department with no staff still appears, but the employee name column shows NULL.

scenes.title: Rewriting as a LEFT JOIN
steps: Change RIGHT JOIN to LEFT JOIN.
Result is identical, easier to read.
scenes.narration: Because right joins are mirrors, any right join can be rewritten as a left join by swapping the table order and keeping the same ON condition. Many teams prefer this so that reading top to bottom always means preserving the first table listed.

scenes.title: The equivalent LEFT JOIN
scenes.code:
SELECT e.name, d.dept_name
FROM departments AS d
LEFT JOIN employees AS e
  ON e.dept_id = d.dept_id;
scenes.narration: This produces exactly the same result as the previous right join. We put departments first and left join employees onto it, so every department is still guaranteed to appear. Standardizing on LEFT JOIN like this keeps a codebase consistent and reduces confusion.

scenes.text: RIGHT JOINs are rare in practice; most engineers reorder tables and use LEFT JOIN for a consistent, readable style.
scenes.narration: Right joins are perfectly valid but uncommon, so prefer reordering the tables and using a left join for a consistent style.
